did: Home's render image had stopped building after the TTS retirement: the page it records needed a package nothing built any more. I reproduced that from a clean checkout and made the image build what that page actually imports, read from its own code instead of a hand-kept list. The whole build now lives in one script, and a new check builds it on every pull request that could break it, the image's own way, so the next such break fails on its pull request instead of on main (RI3; RI1 widened). The full image built and passed its byte proof in the sandbox, after four independent review rounds. Learned: the image's build context is filtered by infra/render/Dockerfile.dockerignore, not the root .dockerignore; Docker itself can run in a cloud session given the proxy's certificate; and an import walk must keep `import { type X }` modules, as TypeScript does.
left: Confirm the render image publishes from main after #2991 merged; then home's render pin can move (server#854, server#739).
